new.title: Climb to the Vogelsburg above the Mainschleife
new.desc: The Vogelsburg is a hilltop site above Volkach, fortified since the Bronze Age and given to Fulda abbey in the 9th century. Count Hermann of Castell turned it into a Carmelite monastery in 1282; today it is a hotel owned mostly by the Juliusspital foundation.
new.tip: Panoramic view over the Main loop and the Volkach vineyards. Reach it on foot from Volkach or Escherndorf.

new.title: See Riemenschneider's Rosary Madonna at Maria im Weingarten
new.desc: The pilgrimage church above Volkach was built 1447-1457 by Kilian Reuter of Würzburg. It holds Tilman Riemenschneider's Rosary Madonna (1521-24), a carved figure about 1.8 m tall that was stolen in 1962 and returned in 1963.
new.tip: The stairway up from Volkach is lined with vineyards. Check opening times with the Volkach tourist office.

new.title: Walk through ancient art at the Knauf Museum Iphofen
new.desc: The Knauf Museum in the old Rentamt on Iphofen's market square opened on 30 June 1983. It shows about 210 plaster casts of major reliefs from Mesopotamia, Egypt, Greece, Rome, ancient America and India.
new.tip: Good for a rainy day; special exhibitions change. Combine with a walk along Iphofen's town wall.

new.title: Look up at the leaning Falterturm of Kitzingen
new.desc: The 52 m Falterturm was built between 1469 and 1496 as a watch tower of the outer town wall. Its crooked helm earned it the name leaning tower of Kitzingen, and local legend blames wine in the mortar.
new.tip: It housed the Deutsches Fastnachtmuseum from 1963 to 2011; the museum now sits in nearby Rosenstraße and Luitpoldstraße buildings.

new.title: Find the world's largest Spitzweg collection in Schweinfurt
new.desc: The Museum Georg Schäfer on Brückenstraße opened on 23 September 2000. It focuses on 19th-century German painting from late Rococo to Impressionism and holds the world's largest Carl Spitzweg collection.
new.tip: Plan 1.5 to 2 hours; check the museum site for opening days.

new.title: Visit the Kunsthalle in Schweinfurt's former swimming bath
new.desc: The Kunsthalle occupies the Ernst-Sachs-Bad, an indoor pool built in the late 1920s to plans by Roderich Fick, reopened as an art museum in 2009. Its permanent display on German art after 1945 stresses Informel, and part of a 17th-century fortification is built into one room.
new.tip: Find it on the Rüfferstraße ring road; allow an hour with the temporary exhibitions.

new.title: Admire the Regentenbau concert hall in Bad Kissingen
new.desc: Max Littmann's neoclassical Regentenbau was inaugurated on 15-16 May 1913. It integrates the older Rossini-Saal (built 1834-38 by Friedrich von Gärtner) and a 200 m arcade in the spa gardens.
new.tip: Walk through the arcade for free; see the Bad Kissingen site for concert dates and tours.

new.title: Visit the Baroque cathedral and Boniface's grave in Fulda
new.desc: Johann Dientzenhofer built the cathedral for Prince-Abbot Adalbert von Schleifras between 1704 and 1712. The relics of Saint Boniface rest in its crypt, a remnant of the earlier Ratgar basilica.
new.tip: Entry to the church is free; the cathedral museum has its own ticket.

new.title: Tour the Stadtschloss with its Hall of Mirrors in Fulda
new.desc: The Stadtschloss was reworked in Baroque style by Johann Dientzenhofer from 1706 to about 1719 and later given a Classicist garden side. The prince-abbot's former dressing room is decorated with hundreds of mirrors.
new.tip: Parts of the palace house city offices; the historic rooms are open for visits at set times.

new.title: Descend into the Carolingian crypt of St Michael's in Fulda
new.desc: St Michael's was built in 820-822 under Abbot Eigil and has a rotunda carried by eight columns. Its crypt, vaulted around a central column with an Ionic capital, is the only part left of the original Carolingian church.
new.tip: Small and quick to visit, next to the cathedral. Check access hours at the parish.

new.title: Stand on Hesse's highest point, the Wasserkuppe
new.desc: At 950 m the Wasserkuppe is the highest mountain in Hesse and the birthplace of gliding: students from Darmstadt flew here from 1911 and Arthur Martens founded the first glider school in 1922. The German Sailplane Museum opened here in 1970.
new.tip: Drive or take the bus up; on clear days you see across the Rhön. The sailplane museum is open April to October.

new.title: Climb the Holy Mountain of the Franconians to Kreuzberg
new.desc: Kloster Kreuzberg was built in 1681-92 for Prince-Bishop Peter Philipp von Dernbach on a pilgrimage mountain at 864 m. It survived secularisation in 1803, and Franciscans still look after the pilgrimage church.
new.tip: Walk the chapel stations of the Cross path from Bischofsheim, then stop at the monastery tavern.
new.q: Kloster Kreuzberg, Bischofsheim an der Rhön

new.title: Roam 120 historic buildings at the Franconian Open-Air Museum
new.desc: The Fränkisches Freilandmuseum in Bad Windsheim was founded in the late 1970s and has more than 120 historic farmhouses, barns and workshops moved here from across Franconia. In autumn it holds an exhibition of old apple varieties.
new.tip: Allow half a day; it is closed in winter, so confirm the season on the museum site.

new.title: Visit the pilgrimage church of Maria im Sand in Dettelbach
new.desc: Pilgrimage here began after a healing at a roadside shrine in 1505. Prince-Bishop Julius Echter began the present church in 1608, consecrated in 1613; the current grace altar dates to 1779.
new.tip: Dettelbach's old town with its town wall is a short walk away.

new.title: Pass through the Maintor into Marktbreit's old town
new.desc: Marktbreit's Maintor of about 1600 is the last of four town gates; it was destroyed in 1945 and rebuilt in 1946-47. The old town is protected as an ensemble, with a Renaissance town hall of 1579-81, the Seinsheim palace of 1585 and the Alter Kranen of 1773.
new.tip: Pair it with a stop at the riverside crane, a short stroll from the gate.

new.title: See the modern abbey church of Münsterschwarzach
new.desc: The Benedictine abbey at the mouth of the Schwarzach into the Main was refounded by missionary monks in 1913-14. The present church by Albert Boßlet dates from 1935-38, and the abbey runs workshops, a book shop and a distillery.
new.tip: Visit the abbey shop for bread, books and schnapps from the monks.

new.title: See the red Kellereischloss in Franconia's oldest wine town
new.desc: Hammelburg has called itself Franconia's oldest wine town since 2002, based on Charlemagne's 777 donation to Fulda abbey that mentions vineyards. The red Kellereischloss was built 1726-31 by Andrea Gallasini, and its cellars once held over 700,000 litres of wine.
new.tip: The wine cooperative's sales rooms are at Kirchgasse 4; their current status is unconfirmed.

new.title: Cross the Main by ferry from Escherndorf to Nordheim
new.desc: The Mainschleife near Volkach has several small river ferries; a walking guide describes the ferryman taking hikers across to Nordheim for a small fee. Ferries stop when the river floods.
new.tip: Check ferry times with the Volkach tourist office (tel. 09381 401300), as they vary by station.

new.title: Ride the summer toboggan run on the Wasserkuppe
new.desc: The Ski- und Rodelarena Wasserkuppe has two roughly 700 m summer toboggan tracks, plus rides such as the Rhönbob. Portals list daily hours of about 10:00 to 17:00, later in Hessian school holidays, depending on conditions.
new.tip: Check the arena site for the day's operation before driving up.

new.title: Fly over the Rhön with the Fliegerschule Wasserkuppe
new.desc: The Fliegerschule Wasserkuppe offers sightseeing flights in motor planes and sailplanes at the cradle of gliding. Paragliding schools also operate on the slopes.
new.tip: Book ahead and check the flight school for conditions.

new.title: Walk the boardwalk across the Schwarzes Moor
new.desc: The Schwarzes Moor is the largest bog complex of the Rhön, about 66 ha at 770-782 m. An oak plank trail of 2.2 km, Bavaria's first bog nature trail (1987), runs across it, with a 17 m lookout tower from 2007.
new.tip: The trail is closed from mid-November to mid-March. The car park is about 300 m from the moor.

new.title: Float in the salt lake of the Franken-Therme
new.desc: The Franken-Therme in Bad Windsheim opened on 16 December 2005. Its Salzsee is fed with brine of about 27 percent salinity and kept near 26 to 30 °C, and there is a sauna world with a snow sauna.
new.tip: Sauna and high-brine areas cost extra.

new.title: Soak in thermal brine at KissSalis Therme
new.desc: KissSalis Therme near Bad Kissingen has about 8,000 sq m of indoor and outdoor pools filled with Bad Kissingen mineral water from the Schönborn fountain, plus a sauna park and brine inhalation.
new.tip: Open daily, roughly 9:00 to 22:00. Check the spa website for current hours.
new.q: KissSalis Therme, Heiligenfelder Allee 16, Bad Kissingen

new.title: Join the Rakoczy-Fest in the Bad Kissingen spa gardens
new.desc: The Rakoczy-Fest is a three-day town festival held on the last weekend of July (24-26 July in 2026), with a parade, music and fireworks. Kurgarten events included dance openings and promenade concerts.
new.tip: Check the Bad Kissingen events page for the next dates.

new.title: Hike the vineyards of the Schwanberg above Iphofen
new.desc: The south-west slopes of the Schwanberg between Iphofen and Rödelsee are among Franconia's best wine sites. The Kappelrangen viewpoint gives views as far as the Rhön, and a platform below Schloss Schwanberg looks over Rödelsee.
new.tip: The TraumRunde Schwanberg starts at the hiking car park near Rödelsee; the Café Schwanberg was reported closed since 2019.

new.title: Eat Sulzfeld's Meterbratwurst at Gasthaus Zum Stern
new.desc: Gasthaus Zum Stern is a family-run inn in a 15th-century timber-framed house at Peuntgasse 5 in Sulzfeld am Main. The menu lists the Sulzfelder Meterbratwurst, roe-deer shoulder with spätzle, and wines from its own vineyard.
new.tip: Phone ahead (09321 13350) to check opening times.
new.q: Gasthaus Zum Stern, Peuntgasse 5, Sulzfeld am Main

new.title: Drink Kreuzberg monastery beer in the Franciscan beer garden
new.desc: The Franciscan monastery has brewed since 1731; it makes about 8,500 hl a year, including Dunkel, Pils, Hefeweizen and a Christmas bock. The beer garden serves Haxen, sauerkraut with dumplings and cheese bread.
new.tip: Gets crowded on sunny weekends. A new brewery building has been under construction since May 2025.
new.q: Klosterbrauerei Kreuzberg, Kreuzberg 1, Bischofsheim an der Rhön

new.title: Taste Iphofen Kronsberg Silvaner at the Zehntkeller
new.desc: The Zehntkeller in Iphofen has been family-run since the early 20th century and farms 27 ha in the Julius-Echter-Berg, Kalb and Kronsberg sites. A restaurant is attached to the hotel and winery.
new.tip: Try the Kronsberg Silvaner, rated 92 points by Falstaff for the 2017 vintage.

new.title: Sip Silvaner at Zur Iphöfer Kammer on the market square
new.desc: A small restaurant at Marktplatz 24 in Iphofen with a short seasonal menu built around the Kammer Silvaner.
new.tip: Right beside the Knauf Museum, so combine a lunch with the museum.

new.title: Settle into a Frankenwein evening at Weinstube Torbäck
new.desc: Weinstube Torbäck sits on Volkach's main street (Hauptstraße 35), in a Mainschleife wine town.
new.tip: Listed hours were about 13:00 to 22:00; verify before you go.

new.title: Pair Fulda beer with local dishes at Hohmanns Brauhaus
new.desc: Hohmanns Brauhaus on Florengasse is a central beer-focused spot in Fulda's old town, serving beer with traditional dishes.
new.tip: Fulda's local specialty is the Ahle Wurscht, which local restaurants serve.

new.title: Order cake at Café Rüttinger in Bad Kissingen
new.desc: Rüttinger is a café and Konditorei at Ludwigstraße 21, rated 4.5 across three review portals.
new.tip: Take a cake or tart break between the spa gardens and the Regentenbau.

new.title: Eat smoked Bratwurst at the Wirtshaus am Kommunbrauhaus
new.desc: The Wirtshaus at Eisweiherweg 1 in Bad Windsheim serves Franconian food and its own beer; the menu lists smoked bratwurst with horseradish and a Franconian Brotzeit platter.
new.tip: Right by the open-air museum, ideal for lunch after a visit.
new.q: Wirtshaus am Kommunbrauhaus, Eisweiherweg 1, Bad Windsheim

new.title: Taste organic wine at Weingut Lange under Schloss Saaleck
new.desc: Weingut Lange - Schloss Saaleck is an organic Naturland estate of over 19 ha near Hammelburg, offering tastings from about 12 to 15 euros and a Schoppenstüble wine tavern.
new.tip: Book tastings in advance.

new.title: Drink house-brewed beer at the Neuschter Biergarten
new.desc: A beer garden at Gartenstraße 31-33 in Bad Neustadt an der Saale with its own brewery, serving German and regional specialities.
new.tip: Check seasonal beer garden hours.
new.q: Neuschter Biergarten, Gartenstraße 31, Bad Neustadt an der Saale

new.title: Try Rhönschaf lamb broth at Brennerei-Gasthaus Dickas
new.desc: Brennerei-Gasthaus Dickas in Bischofsheim lists a lamb broth made from Rhönschaf meat, the regional sheep breed that is the Rhön's mascot.
new.tip: Rhönschaf dishes are showcased in the autumn Genießerwochen.
new.q: Brennerei-Gasthaus Dickas, Bischofsheim an der Rhön
